title: Replica Sampler and Fallback Controller for Non-Intrusive Traffic Observability
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a safe, low-cost pipeline to emit non-intrusive replica (observer) traffic for canary validation and A/B evaluation. The pipeline must support per-tenant credit accounting, prefix-aware sampling, and an automated fallback controller that stops replication for tenants when a cost or SLA threshold is hit. Objective: enable high-fidelity behavioral comparisons between candidate and production model variants without risking tenant quota exhaustion or platform cost surprises.
acceptance_criteria: Ability to route 1% of production requests as observer replicas to a candidate model with <2% added p99 tail latency overhead observed at the gateway
Per-tenant credit usage counters that decrement only for observer tokens and are visible in Console with 1-minute resolution

Circuit-breaker triggers: immediate halt of replication for tenant when monthly observer spend > configured percentage of tenant budget, or when replication causes measurable SLO degradation (latency or 5xx increase)
API and SDK flags to opt-in/out tenants and endpoints for replica observation
Automated rollback/fail-safe that prevents growth of replica traffic during incidents and re-enables replication via a manual accept workflow in Console
design_notes: We will avoid duplicating full request-response flows synchronously. Design is an asynchronous replica stream: gateway emits a compact observation envelope (request metadata, prompt prefix hashes, token budget estimate) to a dedicated observation broker. The broker samples based on prefix heuristics and tenant credits, then enqueues payloads to a candidate serving tier. Return traces and delta metrics are stored in the eval index. Key design points: prefix-aware sampling to prioritize diverse examples, token-estimate-based charge accounting to avoid underestimating cost, and a lease-based execution model so replica jobs are idempotent and can be cancelled mid-flight.
implementation_plan: 1) Add observation envelope emission to API gateway (feat: gateway-observer-v2). Include prefix hash, estimated token count, route metadata, and tenant id.
2) Implement observation broker as separate Kubernetes service. Responsibilities: sampling, tenant-credit checks, enqueue to candidate pool, and circuit-breaker evaluation.
3) Build candidate execution worker with lease semantics and idempotent replay protection. Integrate with runtime-1.22 kernel selection for cost estimates.
4) Extend Console with per-tenant replica spend dashboard and manual circuit-breaker override UI.
5) Add a lightweight SDK flag and HTTP header for customers to enable/disable observer replication on a per-route basis.
6) Integration tests and staged rollout to internal tenants before GA
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: (a) internal-only feature gate with 1 engineering tenant at 0.5% sampling, (b) uplift to 5 internal tenants and 2% sampling after 2 weeks of telemetry, (c) Gradual opt-in for selected customers by request with CLI toggle and manual review. All stages require circuit-breaker thresholds configured (default conservative values) and alerting to SRE. Final GA requires 2-week stability window and accuracy validation against existing eval harness.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope serialization and prefix hashing
Load test broker with synthetic traffic to validate throughput and p99 overhead budgets
End-to-end integration tests: gateway -> broker -> candidate serving -> eval index
Chaos tests: broker pod kills and network partitions to ensure lease cancellation and no duplicate billing
SLO regression tests to ensure replication cannot cause >3% p99 increase for production requests
monitoring_and_metrics: Estimated replica tokens charged vs actual billed tokens
Broker sampling rate and prefix distribution entropy
End-to-end latency delta (replica path relative to baseline)
Errors/5xx from candidate pool and lease failure rate
rollback_criteria: More than 10% of tenants see >5% increase in p99 latency after enabling replication
Any production tenant experiences >$500 unexpected replica spend in 24 hours (configurable)
Unbounded growth in replica queue length for >30 minutes
Repeated lease duplicate executions detected >0.1% of replica jobs
risks: Underestimation of token costs in envelopes leading to tenant budget overruns
Replication-induced resource contention on candidate serving hosts affecting production (misrouted or misconfigured workers)
Complexity of prefix-aware sampling logic causing sampling bias and poor eval coverage
UI confusion: tenants may not realize observer spend is separate from production charges
mitigations: Constrain replica jobs to dedicated candidate pools with lower QoS and strict CPU/GPU quotas
Conservative default sampling rates and token-estimate multipliers to create a safety margin
Exhaustive integration tests and production smoke-tests on internal tenants before customer opt-in
Transparent Console billing view with hourly deltas and email alerting for tenant admins
